commerceSaltTithes.name: Salt Tithes
commerceSaltTithes.flavor: Salt is weighed twice: once for the pot, once for the ledger.
commerceSaltTithes.text: Gain +3 gold per distinct accessible improved luxury you produce. Worked luxury tiles gain +1 food.

theGuildHalls.name: The Guild Halls
theGuildHalls.flavor: A craft is a secret kept in public.
theGuildHalls.text: A city gains +1 production per distinct luxury type it works. Worked camps and plantations gain +1 food.

travellersLetters.name: Travellers' Letters
travellersLetters.flavor: News travels with the cargo, and is worth more.
travellersLetters.text: Your capital gains +2 science and +2 culture, plus +1 of each per foreign empire met, no cap.
travellersLetters.note: An empire you have met stays met, so the letters never stop arriving — a rival you have since destroyed is still a rival you once wrote to.

lettersOfIntroduction.name: Letters of Introduction
lettersOfIntroduction.flavor: A stranger with a letter is not a stranger.
lettersOfIntroduction.text: First contact with each foreign empire grants you 100 gold and that empire 15 gold. Contact recorded before activation cannot pay retrospectively. Discoveries yield 15 gold.
deferred: meeting an empire for the first time pays you, and pays them
lettersOfIntroduction.note: Held whole. The world still does not announce a first meeting. And the grant that pays another empire is a standing line on a town's sheet, where this card wants a one-off paid into a foreign treasury on a single occasion — a windfall banks onto the empire holding the card and knows nothing of a payee.

thePathfindersCompany.name: The Pathfinders' Company
thePathfindersCompany.flavor: Pay the man who knows where the water is.

theLighthouseKeepers.name: The Lighthouse Keepers
theLighthouseKeepers.flavor: A fire on a headland is the cheapest harbour there is.
theLighthouseKeepers.text: Ships gain +1 sight. Lighthouses cost 25% less production; worked fishing boats gain +1 food.

commerceTheAssayersRule.name: The Assayer's Rule
commerceTheAssayersRule.flavor: Every seam weighed, and weighed again.
commerceTheAssayersRule.text: Worked resource tiles that supply gold gain +1 gold.

theMineralTrade.name: The Mineral Trade
theMineralTrade.flavor: Ore that leaves the valley is worth more than ore that stays in it.
theMineralTrade.text: Worked mines and quarries gain +2 gold but lose 1 production.

coastalEstates.name: Coastal Estates
coastalEstates.flavor: The house looks at the water, and the water pays the house.
coastalEstates.text: Worked plantations and fishing boats gain +1 food and +1 gold.

landSpeculation.name: Land Speculation
landSpeculation.flavor: Buy the field before anyone knows what it is for.
landSpeculation.text: Buying a hex with a resource on it grants culture equal to half the gold paid.
landSpeculation.note: The culture is rounded down. The resource must be one your people can see: a resource they have no word for yet does not count.

foundingCapital.name: Founding Capital
foundingCapital.flavor: Somebody has to pay for the first roof, and it is never the settler.

privatePatronage.name: Private Patronage
privatePatronage.flavor: The purse builds faster than the quarry, and asks for its name on the door.
privatePatronage.text: Your cities gain +40% gold. Producing ordinary buildings normally takes 20% more production. Empire buildings and wonders are unaffected.
privatePatronage.note: An ordinary building is one the realm may raise in every city. A wonder is its own kind of queue row, so the slower building does not reach it, and neither does it reach a building the realm may hold only once.

civicReceipts.name: Civic Receipts
civicReceipts.flavor: The town remembers who paid for the roof.
civicReceipts.text: Buying any building grants culture equal to 15% of the gold paid, with no cap.
civicReceipts.note: Every building a town buys pays, however many it has bought before and whichever shelf it came off. What the card still does not pay for is a unit bought at the same counter, which is the whole of what the word building narrows. The share is taken of what actually left the treasury, so a discount at the till is a smaller rebate.

provisioningContracts.name: Provisioning Contracts
provisioningContracts.flavor: Grain moves on paper long before it moves on a cart.
provisioningContracts.text: Domestic routes grant their destination +3 food and +3 production.

theCommonRoad.name: The Common Road
theCommonRoad.flavor: A road belongs to whoever is standing on it.
theCommonRoad.text: Your foreign routes grant you +3 gold, +3 science and +3 culture. Each also grants its host city +3 gold.
theCommonRoad.note: The host's two gold are paid to the foreign city the caravan reaches, and appear on that city's own sheet under this card's name. They are a flat grant: the sea premium and any percentage of yours raise what the trade route pays you, never what it pays your host. A blockade at either end stops both halves, as it stops everything a caravan carries.

theReturnLeg.name: The Return Leg
theReturnLeg.flavor: The cart comes back. Something should be in it.
theReturnLeg.text: Your trade routes between your own towns also pay their origin everything they pay their destination.
theReturnLeg.note: The town a trade route between your own cities leaves is paid what the town it reaches is paid, line for line: the route's own pay, every card's addition to it, and a blockade that stops it. The copy stays in the town it was paid to, and no card that raises what trade routes pay raises it a second time. A trade route to another empire is not copied.

ventureRoutes.name: Venture Routes
ventureRoutes.flavor: The far market pays for the risk of reaching it.
ventureRoutes.text: Your trade routes gain two turns of range. Trade routes between cities at least fifteen hexes apart gain +100% gold.
ventureRoutes.note: The two extra turns are written as a share of the term rather than as a flat figure, because a rule of the simulation takes a percentage and nothing else; at the term the rules table holds today the share comes to exactly the turns the card prints. A renewal rewrites a route's end date, so a road already running gets the longer term from its next renewal on, and the date it started is untouched. The distance is between the two towns and not along the road a cart walks, measured across the map's wrap, so a road that only just qualifies goes on qualifying whoever paves what.

theMerchantLedger.name: The Merchant Ledger
theMerchantLedger.flavor: A name written down is a name you can go back to.
theMerchantLedger.text: Hiring a new caravan costs 15% less. While active, gains +1 science and +1 culture per turn for each distinct destination city first reached by your routes, at most +24 of each.
deferred: every new market your roads reach for the first time teaches and sings, for as long as you keep the ledger
theMerchantLedger.note: Held whole. No book in this game records which markets your caravans have already found.

theFactorsHouses.name: The Factors' Houses
theFactorsHouses.flavor: The factor never leaves. That is the whole of his value.
theFactorsHouses.text: Your cities holding your trading post gain +2 gold and +4 culture.

thePlantersCharter.name: The Planters' Charter
thePlantersCharter.flavor: Break the ground first. The argument can follow.
thePlantersCharter.text: Once drafted, unlock the Plantation House for construction. No chair required. The building is purchased with gold; its payload is specified below.
thePlantersCharter.note: The Plantation House is bought with gold and never built. Every plantation its city works gains a little food and a little gold.

boughtSwords.name: Bought Swords
boughtSwords.flavor: A hired sword is dearer to raise and cheaper to buy.
boughtSwords.text: Your cities gain +38% gold. Military units take 10% more production to train. Purchased units count as trained.

theConvoy.name: The Convoy
theConvoy.flavor: Guard the cart and you are guarding the year.
theConvoy.text: Your combat units within one hex of your trader gain +4 strength. Your traders gain +1 movement. Traders remain plunderable.
theConvoy.note: "Combat units" is the soldiers and the ships, which are two classes on the roster and so two lines here — the escort of a land road and the escort of a sea lane are the same promise made to both. A cart, a workman and a settler are none of them a combat unit and collect nothing.

theTreatyPorts.name: The Treaty Ports
theTreatyPorts.flavor: Two seals on one page, and the harbour opens.
theTreatyPorts.text: +5% production for each empire you hold a deal with, at most +25%.
theTreatyPorts.note: An empire counts once, however many deals you hold with it. A deal that only hands over gold at once leaves nothing running, so it does not count, and a war ends every deal between the two empires.

thePostRiders.name: The Post Riders
thePostRiders.flavor: The road is only as good as the man who rides it at night.
thePostRiders.text: Your civilians and traders beginning a turn on a road you own gain +1 movement for that turn. Hiring and starting a route do not trigger another grant.
deferred: a cart or a workman that wakes on your own road travels further that turn
thePostRiders.note: Held whole. A piece can be paid for the ground it stands on, but the road under it is not among the grounds it can be asked about.

establishedRoutes.name: Established Routes
establishedRoutes.flavor: The second season is worth more than the first.
establishedRoutes.text: A trade route you have kept up for at least twenty turns pays 50% more. A route that lapses, is cancelled or is plundered begins its term again.

theMarketWrit.name: The Market Writ
theMarketWrit.flavor: Where the stalls stand, the writ runs.
theMarketWrit.text: +1 authority for every two Markets in your empire.

commercialEducation.name: Commercial Education
commercialEducation.flavor: A boy who can keep a ledger can keep anything.

strategicReserves.name: Strategic Reserves
strategicReserves.flavor: Keep more than you need, and study what you keep.
strategicReserves.text: Worked strategic resource tiles gain +1 science and +1 gold.

oreCaravans.name: Ore Caravans
oreCaravans.flavor: The valley sells what the valley digs.
oreCaravans.text: Trade routes gain +1 gold for every mine in their origin city.
oreCaravans.note: The mines are counted where the caravan set out, and a mine nobody is working still counts — the coin is for the ore the valley can send, not for the citizens standing in it.

frontierInvestment.name: Frontier Investment
frontierInvestment.flavor: Send the money where the town is still small enough to feel it.
frontierInvestment.text: In your cities of 5 population or fewer, domestic trade routes pay double, and those cities gain +25% gold.
frontierInvestment.note: The doubling is taken of everything already on the cart, and it is asked of the town the trade route ends at. A small town grows out of both halves the turn it passes the mark.

marketFoundations.name: Market Foundations
marketFoundations.flavor: Lay the stones for the stalls, and the town arranges itself around them.
marketFoundations.text: Gain +20% production toward Markets. Markets provide +1 happiness.

financedIndustry.name: Financed Industry
financedIndustry.flavor: Coin buys the tools, and the men who used to eat go and use them.
financedIndustry.text: Cities gain production equal to 30% of their gold yield. Every city loses 3 food.
financedIndustry.note: The share is taken of the town's own flat coin as it stood before any conversion spoke, so a card that turns coin into hammers cannot feed a card that turns hammers into coin.

theHomeMarket.name: The Home Market
theHomeMarket.flavor: Every road that ends here was built for here.
theHomeMarket.text: Cities receiving at least two of your domestic routes gain +30% food, +30% production and +2 happiness, once per city.
theHomeMarket.note: A city has to be the end of two trade routes between your own cities at once, and the contentment is paid once per city however many arrive.

theCaravanseraiNetwork.name: The Caravanserai Network
theCaravanseraiNetwork.flavor: Spread the halts and the desert shrinks.
theCaravanseraiNetwork.text: Each city receiving a domestic trade route grants +2 happiness (once per city); +2 production and +2 gold on domestic trade routes.

theForeignFactor.name: The Foreign Factor
theForeignFactor.flavor: Our man in their market, and their man in ours.
theForeignFactor.text: Each foreign town holding your trading post gives you +1 science and +1 culture for every four of its citizens. Its owner gains +2 gold.
theForeignFactor.note: A trading post is established after a full route term of unbroken trading with a town, and it is yours from then on. A post pays nobody while its holder and the host are at war, or while the host city is blockaded. Each town's citizens are counted on their own, so what is left over in one town does not add to another's. Both halves count the same posts.

theConsulate.name: The Consulate
theConsulate.flavor: A roof, a seal, and somebody who answers letters.
theConsulate.text: Cities holding your established commercial post purchase ordinary buildings and civilian units for 15% less gold, benefiting that city's owner. Each qualifying foreign host also grants you +2 culture while at peace and unblocked. Multiple foreign Consulates do not stack the discount.
deferred: towns where your house is established buy more cheaply, whoever owns them, and each foreign host sings for you
theConsulate.note: Held whole, and now for one reason rather than two. Your trading post is a thing the board records, and the card's second sentence — coin per foreign host, while at peace and unblocked — could be written today. The first sentence cannot: a price is quoted to the empire that is buying, off that empire's own laws, and handing a discount to somebody else is a different seam from paying them a yield.

theWarehouses.name: The Warehouses
theWarehouses.flavor: A full shed is an argument nobody wins.
theWarehouses.text: For each resource of which you control at least 4 copies, double its resource effect and gain +8 culture and +10 gold.
deferred: a good you hold in real quantity pays gold and culture, and works twice as hard
theWarehouses.note: Held whole, and it is the doubling that holds it. Counting the goods the realm holds a shed's worth of is close now that copies are real and countable, though a card still has no way to name its own threshold — the one the game asks about duplicates is fixed. The other half aims a doubling at one named good, where every dial in the vocabulary turns a whole class at once.

thePurpleWorks.name: The Purple Works
thePurpleWorks.flavor: The dye is worth more than the cloth, and the secret more than either.
thePurpleWorks.text: Once drafted, unlock the Purple Works for construction. No chair required. This national building supplies one manufactured luxury copy; its payload is specified below.
deferred: drafting this opens the purple works for building
thePurpleWorks.note: Held whole. The works it would open has not been drawn up yet, and neither has the good it would make.

theMoneyLenders.name: The Money Lenders
theMoneyLenders.flavor: Money left alone is the only servant that never sleeps.
theMoneyLenders.text: Earn interest equal to 4% of your treasury each turn, with no cap.
theMoneyLenders.note: The interest is counted on the treasury after your cities add their gold for the turn and before upkeep is paid. It is paid in whole steps, so the last few coins earn nothing, and a treasury in debt earns nothing.

theCharteredArsenal.name: The Chartered Arsenal
theCharteredArsenal.flavor: Pay on delivery, and inspect before you pay.
theCharteredArsenal.text: Military units purchased with gold gain +4 strength permanently on creation.

luxuryCaravans.name: Luxury Caravans
luxuryCaravans.flavor: One cart of dye is worth ten of grain.
luxuryCaravans.text: Trade routes gain +1 gold for every luxury resource tile in their origin city.
luxuryCaravans.note: Every luxury hex inside the origin's borders counts, worked or not, and two seams of the same good are two — this is a count of ground rather than of the kinds your realm can name.

miningDistricts.name: Mining Districts
miningDistricts.flavor: One shaft is a hole. Six is an industry.
miningDistricts.text: Worked mines gain +2 gold and +2 science for every two adjacent mines.
miningDistricts.note: The neighbours need not be worked and need not be yours; the mine being paid does have to be worked, which is true of every line that lands on a hex. Odd numbers round down, so a mine with three beside it is paid once.

royalAssays.name: Royal Assays
royalAssays.flavor: The assayer's mark turns a rock into a quantity.
royalAssays.text: Each improved luxury resource deposit with a mine provides one additional copy of that luxury.
royalAssays.note: No hex is changed. What grows is the number of copies your realm holds, taken of what your own deposits supply — so a copy another empire lent you is untouched, and a copy you lent away comes off the raised figure rather than being raised with it. A mine is an improvement, so there is no second test for improved. The deposit has to be open to you, like every other seam you count.

theCapitalArsenal.name: The Capital Arsenal
theCapitalArsenal.flavor: The yard never closes, and the yard is here.
theCapitalArsenal.text: There is no limit on the number of units that can be purchased per turn in your capital.
theCapitalArsenal.note: Only the capital, and only the limit: every other refusal at the counter still stands, and a unit still needs somewhere to stand when it arrives.

foreignProcurement.name: Foreign Procurement
foreignProcurement.flavor: Somebody, somewhere, will sell you horses.
foreignProcurement.text: Ignore strategic resource requirements when purchasing units. All units cost 20% more.
foreignProcurement.note: The waiver is for the counter alone — a town still cannot put a knight in its queue without horses. A piece bought this way is an ordinary piece afterwards and still takes a copy, so an empire that buys past its iron finds the iron spoken for.

theHarbourChain.name: The Harbour Chain
theHarbourChain.flavor: Count the harbours and you have counted the fleet.
theHarbourChain.text: Gain +1 route capacity per two Harbours you own, at most +4. Sea routes gain +3 range and +1 gold for every 4 hexes travelled.
theHarbourChain.note: The road per two harbours was written for this card by name and was waiting. The other two sentences needed one word each. A route's pay may now be narrowed by the medium it takes, which is a fact about the road rather than about either of its towns — the same kind of narrowing as which side of a border it crosses, and read the same way — so the coin by the distance is paid on the water and nowhere else. And how far a caravan may be sent by sea joined the short list of figures a law may move, which is the one-line move a route's term already was. The share is taken of the table's own reach and the trading posts' turns are added after it, so the card adds exactly the three turns it prints however many posts the pair holds.

theLeagueOfCities.name: The League of Cities
theLeagueOfCities.flavor: The league is a promise between markets, not between kings.
theLeagueOfCities.text: Cities with one of your paying outgoing routes gain +23% production and cost one less authority, minimum one. Cities without one lose 10% gold.
theLeagueOfCities.note: A paying trade route is simply an active one — a route that has lapsed, been cancelled or been plundered is not counted. The discount never takes a city below one authority and never charges a city that was already free.

theCharterFleet.name: The Charter Fleet
theCharterFleet.flavor: A hull bought is a hull at sea this season.
theCharterFleet.text: Naval combat units cost 20% less gold to purchase. Naval combat units you purchase with gold gain +1 movement permanently. Normal coastal, technology and purchase requirements remain.

exportGuilds.name: Export Guilds
exportGuilds.flavor: The province that sells abroad builds at home.
exportGuilds.text: Each luxury you lend to another empire in a deal gives your capital +4 culture and +2 production.
exportGuilds.note: Each copy counts, so two copies of one luxury lent in two deals count twice. A copy counts while its deal runs, and a war ends every deal between the two empires.

theExchange.name: The Exchange
theExchange.flavor: Two ledgers open on one table is the oldest university there is.
theExchange.text: Each different foreign empire your routes currently serve grants +5% science and culture empire-wide. Foreign routes to your cities grant +2 science and +2 culture to both you and the sender.
theExchange.note: The exchange runs along the trade routes you send: each pays you, and the city it reaches, the same science and culture. A trade route another empire sends to you pays you nothing from this card.

theScholarsRoads.name: The Scholars' Roads
theScholarsRoads.text: Lose 4 route capacity. Your routes gain +2 science and +2 culture, and gain +50% science and culture.

theCustomsHouses.name: The Customs Houses
theCustomsHouses.flavor: The gate that counts you is the gate that knows you.
theCustomsHouses.text: Each customs house in your borders gives its town +4 science and +4 culture, whether or not it is worked.
theCustomsHouses.note: A customs house counts for the town whose borders hold it, whether or not anyone works it.

strategicExports.name: Strategic Exports
strategicExports.flavor: What the forge needs, somebody else needs more.
strategicExports.text: Trade routes gain +2 science per improved strategic resource deposit in their origin city. Your strategic resource deposits provide twice their normal quantity.
strategicExports.note: The beaker on the trade route is an ordinary counted line, asked of the town the caravan left. The doubling touches no ground at all, which is the user's ruling: the seams on the map are what they always were, and what changes is the total your realm holds. It is taken of the copies your own opened seams supply and of nothing else, so a copy another empire lent you is not doubled and a copy you lent away comes off the doubled figure rather than being doubled with it. It is applied outside the walk that is remembered from turn to turn, because that walk is remembered on a clock that does not move when a card is taken up — a law read inside it would leave every count stale for the rest of the turn, and a stale count is a unit a seat can or cannot build, which is how a played game starts disagreeing with a replay of its own log.

purchasedProsperity.name: Purchased Prosperity
purchasedProsperity.flavor: A country that is still buying land is a country that still believes in itself.
purchasedProsperity.text: You may purchase tiles with gold while your authority is negative. If you have purchased a tile in the last 5 turns, all your cities gain +1 happiness.
purchasedProsperity.note: The freeze is lifted for this one counter and nothing else: a hex somebody else owns, a hex none of your towns can reach and a treasury that cannot pay are all still refused. The contentment is a window and not a bill — buying a second hex inside the five turns moves the end date rather than paying again.

civicMarkets.name: Civic Markets
civicMarkets.flavor: The stalls teach arithmetic to everybody who buys anything.

maritimeAuthority.name: Maritime Authority
maritimeAuthority.flavor: The flag over the harbour is the flag over the coast.
maritimeAuthority.text: Gain +3 authority. Naval units gain +5 combat strength against cities.

professionalRetainers.name: Professional Retainers
professionalRetainers.flavor: Men who are paid to fight fight better, and keep being paid.
professionalRetainers.text: All units gain +3 combat strength and cost +1 gold in maintenance.

caravanseraiCities.name: Caravanserai Cities
caravanseraiCities.flavor: One yard in the realm was never enough yards.
caravanseraiCities.text: Caravanserais can be built in every city.
caravanseraiCities.note: Being one to a realm and being one of the realm's great houses were a single mark doing two jobs, and this card is what needed them apart. They are two marks now, and every building that carried the old one carries both, so nothing about any existing row moved. The card lifts the limit and leaves the class exactly where it was: a realm may raise a yard in every town, and every one of them is still a great house — still priced against how many towns it will serve, still admitted wherever a card asks for an empire building, still counted as one of them, and still passed over by a discount written for the ordinary shelves. The card buys many of an expensive thing rather than turning it into a cheap one. One thing had to be made safe alongside it: the walk that gathers what a realm's great houses do used to read each town's shelf in turn, which was harmless while a realm could hold only one of each, so it now reads each row once however many copies stand.

theDyeVats.name: The Dye Vats
theDyeVats.flavor: The colour costs the town its coin and pays it back in song.
theDyeVats.text: Once drafted, unlock the Dye Vats for construction. No chair required. This purchased building turns its city's worked luxuries toward culture and faith; its payload is specified below.
deferred: drafting this opens the dye vats for building
theDyeVats.note: Held whole. The vats they would open have not been drawn up yet, so the charter has nothing to grant.

theEndowment.name: The Endowment
theEndowment.flavor: Buy the roof, and endow the men under it.
theEndowment.text: Purchased buildings provide +2 science each, at most +6 per town.
theEndowment.note: A town now writes down which bank paid for each of its roofs, beside the turn they went up. Either bank counts: a library bought with faith is as bought as one bought with gold. A roof completed in the yard, granted by a card or laid as a relic counts for nothing. A captured town brings its record with it, so a conqueror is paid for the roofs its last owner bought.

thePaidArmy.name: The Paid Army
thePaidArmy.flavor: An army that is paid on time is a cheap army.
thePaidArmy.text: Military-unit upkeep falls by 1 gold, minimum zero. Military units cost 25% less gold to purchase.

merchantPrinces.name: Merchant Princes
merchantPrinces.flavor: Genius is expensive, and the price is quoted.
merchantPrinces.text: Gold may purchase great-person drafts at the existing escalating offer price, with normal availability and purchase limits.

theWorldsExchange.name: The World's Exchange
theWorldsExchange.flavor: The last work of the age is paid for by every market in it.
theWorldsExchange.text: +10% production toward the Opus for each foreign empire your trade routes reach, at most +40%.
theWorldsExchange.note: An empire counts once, however many of your trade routes reach it, and only while one of those routes is running. The bonus goes to the Opus and to nothing else a city builds.

theCharteredMetropolis.name: The Chartered Metropolis
theCharteredMetropolis.flavor: One city, and every road in the world leading to it.
theCharteredMetropolis.text: Cities with at least three of your paying outgoing routes gain +38% food, production and culture, but each costs +4 authority while qualified.
theCharteredMetropolis.note: A paying trade route is simply an active one — a route that has lapsed, been cancelled or been plundered is not counted. A city stops paying the extra authority the moment it drops below three.

theAdmiraltyOfTrade.name: The Admiralty of Trade
theAdmiraltyOfTrade.flavor: The sea has no middle, only two ends.
theAdmiraltyOfTrade.text: Your trade routes to a town holding your trading post have no range limit.
theAdmiraltyOfTrade.note: Only the town the route goes to needs your trading post, and the post must be paying: a war or a blockade suspends the waiver as it suspends a post's income. Routes by land and by sea are treated alike. Nothing else about sending a route changes: a lane no caravan could use, a partner you have not met, a war, a full set of trade routes and a route already running that way are all still refused.

entrenchedInterests.name: Entrenched Interests
entrenchedInterests.flavor: The factors stayed. They always stay.
entrenchedInterests.text: Your units gain +3 combat strength in cities holding your trading post, including foreign cities. Going to war does not remove these posts.
entrenchedInterests.note: Who owns the city is not asked: the line pays in your own towns and in a rival's alike, wherever your trading post stands. The card's second sentence is the rule a post already follows — a post is never removed, by war or by anything else, and war only suspends what a post pays. So this line keeps working against the very empire you established it with.

theMerchantCommonwealth.name: The Merchant Commonwealth
theMerchantCommonwealth.flavor: Govern by ledger and the provinces govern themselves.
theMerchantCommonwealth.text: Each owned city with your established commercial post receiving a domestic route gains +2 happiness and costs one less authority, minimum one.
theMerchantCommonwealth.note: Both halves ask the same two questions of the same town: your trading post stands there, and one of your own trade routes ends there. A town has to answer yes to both, this turn, so a route that lapses takes the contentment and the discount with it while the post itself stays. The discount never takes a city below one authority and never charges a city that was already free.

theMerchantWorks.name: The Merchant Works
theMerchantWorks.flavor: Coin becomes stone, and stone outlasts the coin.
theMerchantWorks.text: Cities building a world wonder, an empire building or the Opus gain production equal to 25% of their gold, and lose 20% of their gold.
theMerchantWorks.note: The last work of all is one of the realm's single great houses by the data's own declaration, so it is covered by the same clause the Forum is. The conversion reads the town's flat coin as it stood before any conversion spoke, which is why the share it pays and the share it costs do not chase each other, and why gold carried home by a foreign road — an empire figure, not a town one — is outside the basis. Only the row at the front of the queue counts: a marvel standing second is a plan.

theGildedScaffold.name: The Gilded Scaffold
theGildedScaffold.flavor: Every marvel has a price. Most of them are simply not quoted.
theGildedScaffold.text: You may purchase world wonders. All your cities lose 15% production.
theGildedScaffold.note: The treasury pays the wonder's full cost in hammers at the ordinary rate, and every other refusal at the counter still stands: a wonder another empire has already claimed, one whose technology is not in, and one whose site the ground does not hold are all refused as before. A wonder is still never bought by the faith bank, except in the one town whose own shelf opens it.

aCourtOfMerchants.name: A Court of Merchants
aCourtOfMerchants.flavor: The chairs nearest the throne were bought, and everyone knows by whom.
aCourtOfMerchants.text: Gain +50% renown, but great-person offers contain only Great Merchants.
aCourtOfMerchants.note: The share is taken of everything the realm earns in renown each turn, and never of a lump a triumph pays. The narrowing is a strong nudge and not a lock: when every great merchant in the world has been called, the draft goes back to showing the whole roster, so a court that has run out of merchants still deals a hand. A draft somebody bought narrowed to another family is dealt as what it was bought as.

cornerTheMarket.name: Corner the Market
cornerTheMarket.flavor: Whoever holds most of the silk sets its price.
cornerTheMarket.text: Commission. Hold four copies of one luxury, counting copies you receive in deals. Then, for the rest of the game, gain +2 happiness for each luxury you hold two or more copies of. The card leaves its chair.

theStrongroom.name: The Strongroom
theStrongroom.flavor: A full vault is a reputation as much as a reserve.
theStrongroom.text: Commission. Goal: end a turn with at least 1,500 gold in your treasury. Reward: culture equal to a fifth of your treasury at that moment, and a great merchant. The card then leaves its chair.

theMapSellers.name: The Map Sellers
theMapSellers.flavor: A good chart is worth the coast it saves you from.
theMapSellers.text: Your capital gains +1 gold and +1 culture for every 40 hexes you have revealed, at most +8 of each.

theCartersGuild.name: The Carters' Guild
theCartersGuild.flavor: The road is laid for the soldiers. The carts use it every other day.
theCartersGuild.text: Towns that receive a domestic trade route build buildings 25% faster.

theNestEgg.name: The Nest Egg
theNestEgg.flavor: Coin you do not spend is coin people talk about.
theNestEgg.text: Your capital gains +1 culture for every 50 gold in your treasury, at most +4.

theStapleRight.name: The Staple Right
theStapleRight.flavor: Every bale passing through must stop here first and be sold.
theStapleRight.text: Gain +3 gold and +2 culture for each luxury you hold two or more copies of.

numidianCavalryCharter.name: Numidian Cavalry
numidianCavalryCharter.flavor: They rode without bridles, and were paid in whatever the caravans carried.
numidianCavalryCharter.text: Once drafted, unlock Numidian Cavalry, a Horseman replacement. No chair required. Gains +1 combat strength per distinct luxury you control; luxuries obtained only through the Silk Road contribute +0.5 instead. Normal technology requirements apply.
numidianCavalryCharter.note: The rider can be built beside the Horseman rather than in place of it, once you reach the age of the Horseman's technology. Every kind of luxury you control counts in full, however you came by it.

housesOfAccount.name: Houses of Account
housesOfAccount.flavor: A ledger well kept is a quiet street.
housesOfAccount.text: Gold buildings provide +2 happiness and +1 renown.

aGuildCommission.name: A Guild Commission
aGuildCommission.flavor: The guild pays for the hall, and expects to be thanked in stone.
aGuildCommission.text: Commission. Goal: buy five buildings with gold while seated. Reward: a free great-person draft, the same offer Merchant Princes sells for gold. The card then leaves its chair.

theMonopoly.name: The Monopoly
theMonopoly.flavor: There is no price but the one we name.
theMonopoly.text: For each luxury you hold three or more copies of and no other empire holds, gain +8 gold, +5 culture and +1 happiness in every city.
theMonopoly.note: The happiness is paid once to your empire for each such luxury, not once in every city.

theCustomsService.name: The Customs Service
theCustomsService.flavor: Everything that leaves is counted, and everything counted is taxed.
theCustomsService.text: Trade routes leaving a city whose borders hold a customs house gain +3 gold and +3 culture.

theBourse.name: The Bourse
theBourse.flavor: Money changes hands here so often it forgets whose it was.
theBourse.text: Gold buildings produce 75% more of their own yields.

patronsAbroad.name: Patrons Abroad
patronsAbroad.flavor: Every house abroad sends something home for the great work.
patronsAbroad.text: Your city building the Magnum Opus gains +3 production for each foreign city holding your trading post.

theMerchantDynasties.name: The Merchant Dynasties
theMerchantDynasties.flavor: The grandfather built the customs house. The grandsons built the library.
theMerchantDynasties.text: Each customs house inside your borders gives its city +3 science and +3 culture, whether or not it is worked.

theSpiceExchange.name: The Spice Exchange
theSpiceExchange.flavor: Pepper bought the ships. The ships bought everything else.
theSpiceExchange.text: Every city gains +5% science and +5% culture for each luxury you hold two or more copies of, at most +30%.

moneyAtWork.name: Money at Work
moneyAtWork.flavor: A full vault builds as surely as a full quarry.
moneyAtWork.text: Every town gains +1 science for every 500 gold in your treasury.

boughtAndPaidFor.name: Bought and Paid For
boughtAndPaidFor.text: Each town gains +4% production and culture for each building you bought there with gold, at most +24%.

theEmbargo.name: The Embargo
theEmbargo.flavor: Trade with us, or trade with nobody.
theEmbargo.text: Rival empires with no trade route to or from you build the Magnum Opus 15% slower.
deferred: rival empires that do not trade with you build the great work more slowly
theEmbargo.note: Held whole. A card of yours cannot yet slow another empire's building, and nothing yet asks whether two empires trade with each other.

theHiredGarrison.name: The Hired Garrison
theHiredGarrison.flavor: The masons cost more than the guards. Hire both.
theHiredGarrison.text: A city with a world wonder or the Magnum Opus at the front of its queue may buy any number of military units with gold each turn.

theNeutralFlag.name: The Neutral Flag
theNeutralFlag.flavor: Both sides need grain, and only one flag can sell it to them.
theNeutralFlag.text: Your trade routes to an empire that is at war with another empire gain +100% gold and +50% science.

theWorldsFair.name: The World's Fair
theWorldsFair.flavor: Bring everything you make, and see everything everyone else makes.
theWorldsFair.text: Commission. Have trade routes to four other empires at the same time. Then your trading post is established in the capital of each of them. The card leaves its chair.
theWorldsFair.note: Each empire counts once, however many of your trade routes reach it. A capital that already holds your established trading post gains nothing more. The new posts pay as any other post does: not during a war, and not while the town is blockaded.

theGreatLoan.name: The Great Loan
theGreatLoan.flavor: Borrow against a future you may never have to pay for.
theGreatLoan.text: When you seat this card, gain gold equal to twenty turns of your gold income. For the next forty turns your cities lose 25% gold. The card then leaves its chair.
theGreatLoan.note: The loan is paid at the end of the turn you seat the card, as long as your gold income is above nothing.

theTradeWinds.name: The Trade Winds
theTradeWinds.flavor: The wind that fills the sails empties the warehouses.
theTradeWinds.text: Gain +3 trade route capacity. Your trade routes reach 50% farther.

marketDay.name: Market Day
marketDay.flavor: Once a week the square is full, and every stall pays its fee.
marketDay.text: Your capital gains +1 gold for every citizen.

theEmporia.name: The Emporia
theEmporia.flavor: Where the fine goods are dug, the merchants build their halls.
theEmporia.text: Improved luxury hexes gain +1 food and +1 production.

theGrainBanks.name: The Grain Banks
theGrainBanks.flavor: The farmer deposits wheat and pays his debts with a written order.
theGrainBanks.text: Cities with a Granary gain +3 gold.

theMarketHalls.name: The Market Halls
theMarketHalls.flavor: A roof over the market, and the market never closes.
theMarketHalls.text: Towns with a Market gain +1 food and +1 production for every three citizens.

namesInStone.name: Names in Stone
namesInStone.flavor: Every donor wants a name over the door.
namesInStone.text: +1% science and culture for every 200 gold you have spent buying this game, at most +30%.
namesInStone.note: Gold counts when you spend it on units, buildings, hexes, caravans and great people, and when you pour it into the Opus. Upgrades, gold given in a deal and gold spent to reroll a draft do not count.

theHanse.name: The Hanse
theHanse.flavor: The towns of the league answer to the league before their lords.
theHanse.text: +3% production and culture for each of your towns holding your trading post, at most +30%.
theHanse.note: A trade route leaves your trading post at both of its ends, so a town counts when one of your routes sets out from it as well as when one arrives. A town counts once your post there is established, and not while the town is blockaded.

billsOfExchange.name: Bills of Exchange
billsOfExchange.flavor: The gold stays in the vault. The paper travels.
billsOfExchange.text: Every town gains +1% production for every 100 gold in your treasury, at most +30%.

theGrainBarges.name: The Grain Barges
theGrainBarges.flavor: The big town eats, and the barges keep coming.
theGrainBarges.text: Your domestic trade routes pay their destination +1 food and +1 production for every four citizens of their origin.

theFondaci.name: The Fondaci
theFondaci.flavor: A house in their harbour, with our name over the door.
theFondaci.text: Each time one of your trading posts is established, gain science and culture, each equal to twenty times the population of its town.
theFondaci.note: A trading post is established after a full route term of unbroken trading with a town. A trade route leaves your trading post at both of its ends, so one route to a new town can establish two posts, and each pays by the size of its own town. A town that already holds your trading post does not establish it again. The moment comes whether or not the post is paying that turn.

theChampagneFairs.name: The Champagne Fairs
theChampagneFairs.flavor: The fair comes round, and the whole province comes to it.
theChampagneFairs.text: Every ten turns, each town that receives a domestic trade route grants culture equal to ten times its population.
theChampagneFairs.note: A fair counts each of your cities that one of your own trade routes reaches on the turn the fair is held, and pays for every citizen living there. The culture goes to your empire. The fairs are counted from the turn you seat the card.

theLinguaFranca.name: The Lingua Franca
theLinguaFranca.flavor: Half of every word is borrowed, and every port understands it.
theLinguaFranca.text: +1% science and culture for every three trade routes running anywhere in the world, at most +30%.
theLinguaFranca.note: Every trade route that is running counts, whoever sent it and wherever it goes, your own included. A route that is renewed is still one route.

commissionTheGreatFair.name: Commission: The Great Fair
commissionTheGreatFair.flavor: Four towns, one market week, and a cart on every road between them.
commissionTheGreatFair.text: Commission. Have domestic trade routes arrive in four of your towns at the same time. Then, for the rest of the game, you may run two more trade routes. The card leaves its chair.
commissionTheGreatFair.note: A town counts while at least one of your trade routes from another of your towns ends there. The goal is checked at the end of each turn.

theCommenda.name: The Commenda
theCommenda.flavor: One partner sails and one stays home, and both own the cargo.
theCommenda.text: Luxuries you lend in a deal count as half a copy for you.
theCommenda.note: The deal still takes the copy, so you can never lend the same copy twice. For your cards and goals, two copies lent count as one copy you hold. A luxury you now hold only through copies you lent still pays you half of its happiness and half of its yields while the deals run.

theCapitulations.name: The Capitulations
theCapitulations.flavor: Their port, our house, and our law inside the door.
theCapitulations.text: Each foreign town holding your trading post lends you one of its luxuries that you lack, at half value.
theCapitulations.note: Only a trading post that is established and paying lends: not during a war with the town's owner, and not while the town is blockaded. Each town lends the first luxury it has improved that you do not hold and that no trade route or other post already brings you, and the towns are taken in the order they were founded. A borrowed luxury pays half of its happiness and half of its yields.

theCasaDaIndia.name: The Casa da Índia
theCasaDaIndia.flavor: Every crate on the quay is weighed, taxed and sold.
theCasaDaIndia.text: Every copy of a luxury you hold pays its yields, not only the first.
theCasaDaIndia.note: Only the luxury's own food, production, gold, science, culture and faith are paid for each copy. Its happiness and every other effect still count once for each kind. Silver and gold already pay some lines for each copy, and those lines are not paid twice.
